description: The Altium schematic editor: placing electrical and drawing objects, connectivity and hierarchy, annotation and the ECO push to the PCB, global editing through the filter/list/inspector panels, mixed-signal simulation with the Simulation Dashboard, and the schematic library editor. Shortcuts shown as P,W are Altium's sequential menu accelerators — press P then W.

tools.name: Place Part (Place > Part)
tools.description: Places a component from the Components panel, a library or the Workspace onto the schematic. Press Tab while the part is on the cursor to edit its designator, comment, parameters and models before placing, Space to rotate and X/Y to mirror. Each click places another instance until Esc.
tools.usage: Place > Part… (P,P); or drag from the Components panel

parameters.name: Designator
parameters.description: Reference designator; leave as R? for automatic annotation later.

parameters.name: Comment
parameters.description: The value shown on the sheet and usually used as the BOM description.

parameters.name: Footprint / Models
parameters.description: Linked PCB footprint, simulation model, signal-integrity model and 3D model.

parameters.name: Part / Pins
parameters.description: Which section of a multi-part component is placed.

tools.example: Press P,P, search 'Res3', press Tab, set Comment to 10k and Designator to R?, place four instances, Esc.

tools.name: Place Wire
tools.description: Draws electrical connections. Altium auto-junctions where a wire ends on another wire and shows a red cross-hair when the cursor is on a valid connection point. Shift+Space cycles the corner mode (90°, 45°, any angle, arc) and Space flips the corner direction while drawing.
tools.usage: Place > Wire (P,W or Ctrl+W)
tools.example: Ctrl+W, click U1 pin 3, Shift+Space to switch to 45° corners, click the corner, click R5 pin 1, right-click to end.
tools.notes: A wire drawn with Place > Line looks identical but carries no connectivity — check the Properties panel if a connection is not being made.

tools.name: Place Bus and Bus Entry
tools.description: Draws a bus and the short entries that attach wires to it. As in most EDA tools the bus is graphical: connectivity comes from net labels such as D[0..7] on the bus and D0..D7 on the branch wires. The compiler checks that branch labels are members of the bus range and reports mismatches.
tools.usage: Place > Bus (P,B); Place > Bus Entry (P,U)
tools.example: P,B draw the bus; P,N label it D[0..7]; P,U place entries; P,N label each branch wire D0, D1 …

tools.name: Place Net Label
tools.description: Names a net. Identically named net labels are connected according to the project's Net Identifier Scope: in a flat design they connect across all sheets, in a hierarchical design only within a sheet. Placing a label whose text ends in a digit auto-increments on each subsequent placement.
tools.usage: Place > Net Label (P,N); press Tab to set the text before placing
tools.example: P,N, Tab, text 'D0', place on the first branch wire — subsequent placements offer D1, D2, …
tools.notes: A net label must actually touch the wire; a label floating near a wire names nothing and the compiler reports 'Net label not connected'.

tools.name: Place Port
tools.description: Creates a connection point at the sheet boundary that maps to a sheet entry on the parent sheet symbol, which is how a hierarchical design connects. The port's name must match the sheet entry's name, and its I/O type (Input, Output, Bidirectional, Unspecified) feeds the connection-matrix checks.
tools.usage: Place > Port (P,R)

parameters.name: Name
parameters.description: Must match the corresponding sheet entry on the parent sheet symbol.

parameters.name: I/O Type
parameters.description: Input, Output, Bidirectional or Unspecified, checked by the Connection Matrix.

parameters.name: Harness Type
parameters.description: Set when the port carries a signal harness rather than a single net.

tools.example: On child.SchDoc place a port 'VOUT' with I/O Type Output; on the parent sheet symbol add a sheet entry 'VOUT' with I/O Type Output.

tools.name: Place Power Port
tools.description: Places a global power or ground symbol whose Net name connects everywhere in the project regardless of hierarchy scope. The style (Bar, Wave, Power Ground, Signal Ground, Earth, GOST variants, Arrow, Circle) is purely graphical; only the Net property matters electrically.
tools.usage: Place > Power Port (P,O); press Tab to set Net and Style
tools.example: P,O, Tab, Net '+3V3', Style 'Bar', place on each supply pin; repeat with Net 'GND', Style 'Power Ground'.
tools.notes: Power ports are always global. If two supplies must stay separate, give them different net names rather than relying on hierarchy.

tools.name: Place Sheet Symbol and Sheet Entry
tools.description: Builds hierarchy. A sheet symbol on the parent sheet references a child schematic through its File Name property; sheet entries on its edge correspond by name to ports inside the child. Design > Create Sheet Symbol From Sheet generates the symbol and all its entries automatically from an existing child sheet.
tools.usage: Place > Sheet Symbol (P,S); Place > Add Sheet Entry (P,A); Design > Create Sheet Symbol From Sheet or Ctrl+drag to synchronise

parameters.name: Designator
parameters.description: The instance name of the block; it prefixes flattened designators in multi-channel designs.

parameters.name: File Name
parameters.description: Child schematic document the symbol refers to.

parameters.name: Repeat(...)
parameters.description: Multi-channel syntax such as `Repeat(CH, 1, 8)` that instantiates the child sheet eight times.

tools.example: Design > Create Sheet Symbol From Sheet > choose amp.SchDoc; the symbol appears with a sheet entry for every port in the child.

tools.name: Multi-channel design (Repeat)
tools.description: Instantiates one child sheet many times by writing `Repeat(<name>, <first>, <last>)` in a sheet symbol's designator and `Repeat(<net>)` on the sheet entries that must be bussed out. The compiler flattens this into the full channel set, and the PCB side gets matching rooms and component classes plus Place > Replicate-style room copying.
tools.usage: Sheet symbol Designator: `Repeat(CH,1,8)`; sheet entry name: `Repeat(IN)`; set Project Options > Multi-Channel naming
tools.example: Designator `Repeat(CH,1,8)`, File Name channel.SchDoc, entry `Repeat(AUDIO_IN)` — compiling produces CH1..CH8 with designators like R1_CH3.
tools.notes: The designator format for flattened channels is set on Project Options > Multi-Channel; changing it after layout renames every component.

tools.name: Place Off-Sheet Connector
tools.description: Connects nets between sheets that sit at the same level of a flat design, as an alternative to global net labels. Two off-sheet connectors with the same name join into one net. Useful when the Net Identifier Scope is hierarchical but a few signals still need to hop sheets.
tools.usage: Place > Off Sheet Connector
tools.example: Place an off-sheet connector named 'RESET_N' on both sheet 2 and sheet 5 of a flat design.

tools.name: Place Junction (manual junction)
tools.description: Forces a connection dot where wires cross. Altium places junctions automatically at T intersections; a manual junction is only needed for a genuine four-way crossing connection, which most design standards discourage in favour of two staggered T junctions.
tools.usage: Place > Manual Junction
tools.example: Place > Manual Junction at the crossing of the two supply wires that really must connect.

tools.name: Place Directives (No ERC, Parameter Set, Compile Mask, Blanket, Probe)
tools.description: Small annotations that modify how the compiler and other tools treat part of a schematic. No ERC (the red X) suppresses violations on a pin or net; Parameter Set attaches design-rule or class parameters to a net so PCB rules are driven from the schematic; Compile Mask excludes an area from compilation; Blanket applies a directive to every object it covers; Probe marks a net for simulation or for the PCB's Board Insight.
tools.usage: Place > Directives > No ERC (P,V,N) / Parameter Set / Compile Mask / Blanket / Probe

parameters.name: No ERC
parameters.description: Suppresses compiler violations on the object it is placed on; can be restricted to specific error types.

parameters.name: Parameter Set
parameters.description: Carries name/value pairs, commonly `Rule = Width(…)` or a net class assignment, into the PCB.

parameters.name: Compile Mask
parameters.description: Greys out and excludes a region so unfinished circuitry does not generate errors.

tools.example: P,V,N on every unused microcontroller pin to clear the 'Net has no driving source' warnings; add a Parameter Set on VBUS carrying `Rule = Width(Min=20mil, Preferred=30mil, Max=50mil)`.

tools.name: Place Text String / Text Frame / Note
tools.description: Documentation objects. A text string is a single line, a text frame is a bordered multi-line block with word wrap, and a Note is a collapsible sticky note that can be shown as an icon until clicked. None affect connectivity; special strings like `=CurrentDate` or `=DocumentName` resolve at print time.
tools.usage: Place > Text String (P,T); Place > Text Frame (P,F); Place > Notes > Note
tools.example: Place a text frame with the power-sequencing requirements next to the supply block; add a Note reminding the layout engineer to keep the sense trace short.

tools.name: Drawing objects (Line, Polygon, Arc, Ellipse, Rectangle, Bezier, Image)
tools.description: Non-electrical graphics for grouping, emphasis and documentation: Line, Polyline, Polygon, Arc, Elliptical Arc, Ellipse, Rectangle, Round Rectangle, Pie Chart, Bezier and embedded Image. They are also the drawing primitives used inside the schematic library editor to build symbol bodies.
tools.usage: Place > Drawing Tools > Line / Polygon / Arc / Ellipse / Rectangle / Bezier / Graphic…
tools.example: Place > Drawing Tools > Rectangle around the isolated section, set the fill to a pale colour and Draw Solid off so the circuit stays readable.

tools.name: Annotate Schematics
tools.description: Assigns reference designators across the project. The dialog chooses the processing order (up-then-across, across-then-down, etc.), the matching parameters used to pack multi-part components, and the scope, then shows the proposed changes before applying them through an ECO. Variants of the command cover quiet, forced, reset and board-level annotation.
tools.usage: Tools > Annotation > Annotate Schematics… / Annotate Schematics Quietly / Force Annotate All Schematics / Reset Schematic Designators / Back Annotate Schematics / Board Level Annotate

parameters.name: Order of Processing
parameters.description: Up then Across, Across then Down, Down then Across, Across then Up.

parameters.name: Matching Options
parameters.description: Which parameters must match for two parts to be packed into one physical component.

parameters.name: Schematic Sheets To Annotate
parameters.description: Per-sheet enable plus the designator index start for each sheet.

tools.example: Tools > Annotation > Annotate Schematics > order 'Across then Down' > Update Changes List > Accept Changes (Create ECO) > Execute Changes.
tools.notes: Force Annotate renumbers everything and will break the link to an existing PCB — use the normal Annotate, which only fills in unannotated parts.

tools.name: Back Annotate Schematics / Board Level Annotate
tools.description: Brings designator changes made on the PCB back into the schematic. Board Level Annotate renumbers the board by physical position (left-to-right, top-to-bottom) so the assembly drawing reads sensibly, and Back Annotate Schematics then pushes those designators back through an ECO so the two domains agree.
tools.usage: Tools > Annotation > Board Level Annotate… (PCB); Tools > Annotation > Back Annotate Schematics (schematic)
tools.example: On the PCB: Tools > Annotation > Board Level Annotate > order by position > Apply; on the schematic: Back Annotate Schematics > Execute Changes.

tools.name: Update PCB Document (forward ECO)
tools.description: The forward path from schematic to board: it compares the validated schematic with the PCB and generates change orders for added, removed and modified components, nets, classes, rooms, parameters and schematic-defined rules. The ECO dialog shows every change for review before Execute applies it.
tools.usage: Design > Update PCB Document <board>.PcbDoc (from the schematic editor)
tools.example: Design > Update PCB Document board.PcbDoc > Validate Changes > Execute Changes; new components appear beside the board outline ready to place.
tools.notes: Validate the project first — an uncompiled schematic produces an incomplete or empty change list.

tools.name: Import Changes from PCB (reverse ECO)
tools.description: The reverse path: changes made on the PCB (designators, footprints, net names, classes) are compared with the schematic and pushed back as change orders. Together with Update PCB Document it keeps the two domains synchronised without any netlist file.
tools.usage: Design > Import Changes From <project>.PrjPcb (from the PCB editor)
tools.example: After Board Level Annotate: Design > Import Changes From board.PrjPcb > Validate > Execute — the schematic designators now match the board.

tools.name: Netlist for Project / for Document
tools.description: Exports the connectivity in a foreign netlist format for third-party tools: Protel, PADS, CadnetiX, EDIF, Verilog, VHDL, SPICE and many more. Within Altium itself netlists are never needed because the ECO mechanism carries connectivity, so this exists purely for interoperability.
tools.usage: Design > Netlist for Project > <format>; Design > Netlist For Document > <format>
tools.example: Design > Netlist for Project > Protel — the .NET file is written into the project's Generated folder.

tools.name: Find Similar Objects
tools.description: The core of Altium global editing. Right-clicking an object opens a dialog listing every one of its properties with Any/Same/Different matchers; choosing Same on the properties that matter selects every object that matches and opens the SCH Inspector so they can all be edited at once. It is how you change every 0603 resistor's comment or every port's font in one step.
tools.usage: Right-click an object > Find Similar Objects… (or Shift+F); set matchers, tick Select Matching and Open Inspector
tools.example: Right-click a net label > Find Similar Objects > Object Kind = Same, Font = Any > Select Matching > in the Inspector set Font Size to 10 for all of them.

tools.name: SCH Inspector panel
tools.description: Shows and edits the properties common to all currently selected schematic objects. Typing a value into a field applies it to every selected object, which is the standard bulk-edit mechanism after a Find Similar Objects or a filter selection.
tools.usage: View > Panels > SCH Inspector (F11 in many configurations)
tools.example: Select 40 resistors, open SCH Inspector, set 'Comment' to 10k — every selected part updates at once.

tools.name: SCH Filter panel
tools.description: Selects schematic objects with a query expression rather than by clicking. Queries such as `IsPart and Comment = '10k'` or `InNet('GND')` select, zoom to, mask or highlight the matching set. The same query language drives design rules and the PCB filter.
tools.usage: View > Panels > SCH Filter; type a query and press Apply
tools.example: Query: `IsPart And (Designator Like 'R*')` > Apply with 'Select' ticked to grab every resistor in the project.

tools.name: SCH List panel
tools.description: A spreadsheet of the selected or filtered schematic objects, one row per object and one column per property. In Edit mode cells can be typed into directly, making it the most efficient way to review and repair many objects at once, and it supports copy/paste with Excel.
tools.usage: View > Panels > SCH List; switch the panel mode to Edit and the scope to 'all objects' or 'selected objects'
tools.example: Filter every port, open SCH List in Edit mode, and fix the I/O Type column for the ports that are set to Unspecified.

tools.name: Smart Paste
tools.description: Pastes clipboard contents with a conversion applied: net labels into ports, ports into sheet entries, sheet entries into ports, pins into net labels, or a paste array that replicates the clipboard n times with a spacing and a designator/net-name increment. It turns tedious re-typing into one dialog.
tools.usage: Edit > Smart Paste… (Ctrl+Shift+V)

parameters.name: Paste As
parameters.description: Target object type: Ports, Net Labels, Sheet Entries, Harness Entries, Cross Sheet Connectors, etc.

parameters.name: Paste Array
parameters.description: Item count, text increment and horizontal/vertical spacing for repeated placement.

tools.example: Copy the ports from the child sheet, then on the parent sheet symbol Edit > Smart Paste > Paste as: Sheet Entries — every entry is created with matching names and I/O types.

tools.name: Selection Filter
tools.description: Controls which object kinds the mouse can select, from the Properties panel when nothing is selected. Turning off Wires and Parts while tidying graphics (or the reverse) removes the frustration of grabbing the wrong object in a dense schematic. The PCB editor has the equivalent control.
tools.usage: Properties panel (nothing selected) > Selection Filter; or the Selection Filter button on the Active Bar
tools.example: Untick everything except 'Text' so a drag-select over the sheet picks up only the annotation text.

tools.name: Sheet templates and title blocks
tools.description: A schematic template (.SchDot) supplies the sheet border, title block graphics and default parameters to every document that uses it. Special strings (`=Title`, `=DocumentNumber`, `=Revision`, `=SheetNumber`, `=SheetTotal`, `=CurrentDate`, `=ProjectName`) resolve from document and project parameters at display and print time, so one template serves every sheet.
tools.usage: Design > Templates > Set Template from File / Update Current Document; parameters at Project > Project Options > Parameters and in the Properties panel > Parameters
tools.example: Design > Templates > Set Template from File > company_A3.SchDot > apply to 'All documents in the project'; set the project parameter 'Revision' to B and every title block updates.

tools.name: Document Options (Properties with nothing selected)
tools.description: The active schematic's own settings: sheet size and orientation, units, visible and snap grids, border and title-block display, document parameters, and the Selection Filter. Getting the snap grid right (100 mil is the classic pin pitch) is what makes wires meet pins reliably.
tools.usage: Click empty sheet space > Properties panel (General, Parameters and Page Options tabs)
tools.example: Properties > Page Options > Sheet Size A3, Orientation Landscape; General > Snap Grid 100 mil, Visible Grid 100 mil.

tools.name: Simulation Dashboard
tools.description: The front end for Altium's built-in mixed-signal SPICE simulator. It checks that every component has a simulation model and that the sources and ground are present, then configures and runs the analyses — Operating Point, DC Sweep, AC Sweep, Transient, Noise, Transfer Function, Temperature Sweep, Parameter Sweep and Monte Carlo — and opens the results in the SimData viewer.
tools.usage: Simulate > Simulation Dashboard (schematic editor, project validated)

parameters.name: Verification
parameters.description: Reports components without a simulation model, missing supplies and missing ground before a run.

parameters.name: Preferences
parameters.description: Integration method, accuracy and per-analysis SPICE options.

parameters.name: Analysis setup
parameters.description: Per-analysis parameters plus which signals to record as outputs.

tools.example: Simulation Dashboard > Verification: Check > fix the two parts without models > AC Sweep: 10 Hz to 10 MHz, 100 pts/decade, output V(OUT) > Run.
tools.notes: The dashboard's verification step catches the overwhelming majority of 'the simulation will not run' problems before the solver is even started.

tools.name: Simulation models and .MODEL/.SUBCKT links
tools.description: Each simulatable component carries a Simulation model in its Models list, linking it to a generic model (Resistor, Capacitor, Diode, BJT, MOSFET …) with parameters, or to a SPICE subcircuit in a .ckt/.mdl file with its pin mapping. Vendor SPICE models are added by attaching the file and mapping the symbol pins to the subcircuit's node order.
tools.usage: Component Properties > Models > Add > Simulation; choose Model Kind, Model Sub-Kind, Model Name and the netlist template / port map
tools.example: Add a Simulation model of kind 'Spice Subcircuit', browse to opamp.ckt, select the .SUBCKT, and map pins 1,2,3 to IN+, IN-, OUT.
tools.notes: A mismatched port map produces a simulation that runs but gives nonsense — always check the subcircuit's documented node order.

tools.name: Simulation sources and probes
tools.description: The Simulation Sources library supplies the stimulus parts (VSRC/ISRC with DC, AC and transient specifications for SIN, PULSE, PWL, EXP and SFFM, plus dedicated VSIN, VPULSE, VPWL parts) and the initial-condition and node-set parts. Probes and the .IC/.NS parts mark what is recorded and how the solver starts.
tools.usage: Place from the Simulation Sources / Simulation Special Function libraries; set the DC, AC and transient parameters in the Properties panel
tools.example: Place VSIN with Amplitude 1 V, Frequency 1 kHz, DC Magnitude 0, AC Magnitude 1 — the same source drives both the transient and the AC sweep.

tools.name: SimData waveform viewer
tools.description: Displays simulation results in a .sdf document: multiple plots and waves, cursors with measurement readouts, arithmetic expressions on waveforms, FFT, and per-run traces for parameter sweeps and Monte Carlo. Waveforms can be added, grouped, scaled and exported to CSV for external analysis.
tools.usage: Opens automatically after a run; Wave menu / right-click for Add Wave, Add Wave to Plot, Cursors, Measurement Cursors
tools.example: In the SimData document right-click > Add Wave > expression `v(out)/v(in)` > enable measurement cursors to read the -3 dB point.

tools.name: Schematic Library Editor
tools.description: Creates and edits schematic symbols in a .SchLib. A component holds one or more parts (sections), each drawn with the drawing tools and given pins; the component's Models list links the footprint, simulation, signal-integrity and 3D models, and its Parameters carry the BOM data. The SCH Library panel lists the components, their parts, pins and models.
tools.usage: File > New > Library > Schematic Library; View > Panels > SCH Library; Tools > New Component
tools.example: Tools > New Component 'LM358', Place > Pin for each terminal, Tools > New Part for the second op-amp section, Models > Add > Footprint > SOIC-8.
tools.notes: Use Tools > Update Schematics to push a library symbol change into designs that already use it.

tools.name: Symbol Wizard
tools.description: Generates a rectangular symbol from a table of pin numbers, names and electrical types, with layout options (single-part, quad, line, dual) and the ability to paste the pin table straight from a datasheet's spreadsheet. It turns a 144-pin MCU symbol from an hour of clicking into a couple of minutes.
tools.usage: Schematic Library Editor > Tools > Symbol Wizard…

parameters.name: Number of Pins / Layout Style
parameters.description: Pin count and arrangement (Single Part, Dual, Quad, Line of pins).

parameters.name: Pin table
parameters.description: Position, Display Name, Designator, Electrical Type, Description — pasteable from Excel.

tools.example: Tools > Symbol Wizard > paste 64 rows from the datasheet spreadsheet > Layout: Quad > Place Symbol.

tools.name: Place Pin (library editor)
tools.description: Adds a pin to a library symbol. Key properties are Designator (the package pin number), Display Name (the function name), Electrical Type (Input, Output, I/O, Open Collector, Open Emitter, Passive, HiZ, Power) which drives the connection matrix, Length, and symbol decorations (Dot for inversion, Clock, Active Low In/Out).
tools.usage: Schematic Library Editor > Place > Pin (P,P); press Tab to edit before placing

parameters.name: Electrical Type
parameters.description: Feeds the Connection Matrix checks; Power pins are also what hidden-pin power connection relies on.

parameters.name: Hide
parameters.description: Hides a power pin and connects it to a named net — legacy behaviour that hides real connectivity; prefer visible power pins.

parameters.name: Swapping options
parameters.description: Pin and part swap groups used by Board Level annotation and pin/gate swapping on the PCB.

tools.example: Place > Pin, Tab, Designator 8, Display Name VCC, Electrical Type Power, Length 300 mil, place on the top edge.
tools.notes: Avoid hidden power pins in new libraries: they connect invisibly and cause surprises when the net name differs from the design's supply name.

tools.name: Model links (Footprint, Simulation, Signal Integrity, PCB3D)
tools.description: The Models list on a component binds it to its physical and analytical representations: one or more PCB footprints (with one current), a simulation model, a signal-integrity model (device type and pin models for reflection and crosstalk analysis), and a 3D model. Multiple footprints allow a part to be assembled in different packages without changing the symbol.
tools.usage: Component Properties > Models > Add > Footprint / Simulation / Signal Integrity / PCB3D
tools.example: Add footprints SOT-23-5 and SC70-5 to the regulator symbol; the designer picks which is current per placement from the Properties panel.

tools.name: Component Wizard (library)
tools.description: Walks through creating a component with a standard body style and pin arrangement, filling in designator prefix, part count and pin properties. It is the quick path for conventional devices; the Symbol Wizard is better for large pin tables.
tools.usage: Schematic Library Editor > Tools > Component Wizard…
tools.example: Tools > Component Wizard > style: rectangle > 14 pins > designator prefix U > finish, then adjust pin names.

tools.name: Update Schematics / Update Schematic Sheets
tools.description: Pushes changes made to a library symbol into the designs that already use it, through an ECO so the change list is reviewable. Without it, editing a library leaves existing placements untouched — the symbol on the sheet is a copy.
tools.usage: Schematic Library Editor > Tools > Update Schematics (or right-click a component in the SCH Library panel > Update Schematics)
tools.example: Fix a wrong pin number in company.SchLib > Tools > Update Schematics > review the ECO > Execute Changes.

tools.name: Electrical Rule Check (compiler violations)
tools.description: Altium's schematic ERC is not a separate command: it runs as part of project validation, driven by the Error Reporting page (duplicate designators, floating net labels, unconnected pins, nets with no driving source, bus range mismatches, port/sheet-entry mismatches, and dozens more) and the Connection Matrix (pin-type-to-pin-type legality). Each violation has its own severity from No Report to Fatal Error.
tools.usage: Project > Project Options > Error Reporting and Connection Matrix; run with Project > Validate PCB Project
tools.example: Set 'Nets with no driving source' to Warning and 'Duplicate Component Designators' to Fatal Error, then validate; the Messages panel lists everything.
tools.notes: Suppress individual legitimate cases with a No ERC directive rather than by lowering a rule's severity for the whole project.

tools.name: Cross Probe
tools.description: Jumps from an object in one editor to the matching object in the other: click a component or net on the schematic and the PCB editor zooms to and highlights the corresponding component or net, and vice versa. Unlike Cross Select Mode it is a one-shot command rather than a persistent selection link.
tools.usage: Tools > Cross Probe (Ctrl+double-click also cross-probes in many configurations)
tools.example: On the PCB, Tools > Cross Probe then click a component — the schematic jumps to that symbol.

tools.name: Compile Mask and compiled document view
tools.description: After validation, Altium can show a document in its compiled form, with sheet symbols expanded into channels, parameter special strings resolved and variant not-fitted parts crossed out. Compile masks exclude unfinished areas from the build so work in progress does not drown the Messages panel.
tools.usage: Place > Directives > Compile Mask; switch documents in the Projects panel's compiled hierarchy after validation
tools.example: Draw a compile mask over the half-finished test circuit, validate the project, and only the real design's errors are reported.

tools.name: Place Probe (schematic)
tools.description: Marks a net for observation. In simulation a probe selects a signal to record; combined with the PCB's Board Insight and cross-probing it also acts as a design annotation pointing at a signal of interest. Probes are placed like directives, on a wire or pin.
tools.usage: Place > Directives > Probe; or add probes from the Simulation Dashboard's output list
tools.example: Place a probe on the feedback node so the transient run records it without saving every internal node.
